verdict.headline: Pangram caught most fakes overall, but one forger model slipped past it 4 times out of 5, and government-report rewrites fooled it half the time.
findings: Across all 112 attack attempts, Pangram caught 86.6% on the first pass, but 33.9% eventually evaded detection.
GLM 5.3 Flash (n=22) evaded detection 81.8% of the time overall, and evaded on 100.0% of its gov_report attempts.
Hermes-3 8B (n=30) was caught_first 100.0% of the time, with 0.0% evaded across all three document types.
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (n=30) evaded only 13.3% overall, but by-document results varied: 0.0% on 1709.02445v2 vs 20.0% on both court_romanko_2014 and gov_report.

False alarms on real human text were rare (1 of 30 genuine documents flagged, 3.3% false_alarm_pct overall), but evasion itself varied sharply by document: 11.8% for the science paper (1709.02445v2) vs 50.0% for the government report.
advice: Don't treat one detector's score as proof either way: GLM 5.3 Flash (n=22) evaded Pangram 81.8% of the time, while Hermes-3 8B (n=30) evaded it 0.0% of the time -- results depend heavily on which model wrote the text.
Weigh results by document type, not just an average: evaded ranged from 11.8% on the science paper to 50.0% on the government report in this test.
Note sample sizes before trusting a leaderboard row: GLM 5.3 Flash's figures come from only 22 attempts versus 30 for the other three models, so its numbers are less stable.
